text:
Lia G: heads-up — escalation from Acme (prod) about embeddings perf regression after the runtime patch deployed ~22:00 UTC last night. They say vectors/sec dropped dramatically for bulk workloads. attaching initial numbers they sent.

support-bot: ticket #INC-7123 created (severity: high) and linked to this thread.

Lia G: customer metrics: previously ~48k vectors/sec (steady), now ~9k–14k depending on time window. They batch ~1.8k texts per request (we think they're doing multiple smaller batches), model = embed-analog-2.7b-quant, route = hosted-us-west-2.

Omar K: do we have recent changes that could affect batching or kernel selection? I pushed the continuous-batching_v2 runtime tweak yesterday (patch rrt-2026-11).

Sasha R: I briefly looked at telemetry — there's a jump in "embedding_queue_depth" and "avg_batch_size" dropped. Also the token/sec metric is flat-ish but vectors/sec collapsed, which smells like a path that generates vectors slower per request (maybe FP32 fallback or CPU memcpy).

Lia G: customer also reported sporadic "DimensionMismatch" errors in some requests (not everywhere). Example payload snippet they sent: 
```
{"input": ["... 1800 strings ..."], "model": "embed-analog-2.7b-quant", "expected_dim": 1536}
```
They said their client expects 1536 dims but model produces 1024 normally — possibly old client config. They think that mismatch started after our change because before that the client hit higher throughput (weird).

Omar K: Dimension mismatch would cause the client to re-encode/transpose on host side? If the server returns metadata mismatch and client tries to remap, that could slow end-to-end, but wouldn't explain a global vectors/sec drop across many customers.

Sasha R: agree. I pulled a perf sample from the runtime around deploy window. Snapshot: 
```
# runtime perf (summary)
time: 2025-11-20T22:12:01Z
model: embed-analog-2.7b-quant
avg_vectors_per_sec: 11,200
avg_gpu_util: 42%
avg_batch_size: 37
queue_depth_95p: 820
```
Sasha R: compare to pre-deploy: avg_vectors_per_sec ~48k, gpu_util ~88%, avg_batch_size ~128, queue_depth_95p ~120. So after deploy: lower batch size, bigger queue depth. Looks like batching collapsed and queue grew — odd.

Lia G: customer observed increased latency tail and more timeouts. They saw many requests sitting in our "prepare" stage before dispatch. Could be a blocking op in the prepare path.

Omar K: I'm suspecting the new batching logic added a conservative aggregation timer that reduces batch window when request sizes are large, causing smaller batches and lower throughput. If avg_batch_size fell from ~128 to ~37, vectors/sec would drop proportionally.

eng-oncall: adding logs from one affected host: 
```
[22:11:58] host-37 prepping request id=abc123 size=1796 tokens=~88
[22:11:58] host-37 batcher: enqueue -> queue_len=812
[22:12:00] host-37 batcher: timer fired (timeout_ms=6) batching -> batched_count=32
[22:12:00] host-37 runtime: kernel_select -> chosen=generic_fp32_path (fallback)
[22:12:03] host-37 runtime: dispatched to GPU id=0 seq=... exec_ms=230
```
eng-oncall: note the kernel_select fallback to generic_fp32_path — that could explain GPU util being low (kernel less efficient) and exec_ms up. We should check why optimized quantized kernels weren't picked.

Sasha R: possible triggers for kernel fallback: model artifact mismatch (quant params missing), a guardrail in kernel selector when batch shapes vary too much, or a driver/CUDA mismatch. Is there a recent libcudnn/libtorch bump in the deploy?

Omar K: rrt-2026-11 included a small cuDNN bump and a change to kernel-selector heuristics to prefer safety checks for out-of-bounds quant params. If that changed to prefer safe path for edge cases, it could route many requests to slow path. We'll roll back that heuristics change on a canary.

Lia G: meanwhile, we need a reproducible test to confirm. Sasha, can you share a repro script we can run on a canary host that approximates the customer's traffic?

Sasha R: yes — quick perf curl harness (single-host):
```bash
# run a tight loop that mimics their batch sizes
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-analog-2.7b-quant","input": ["lorem ipsum" for j in range(1800)]}' &\
done
# measure vectors/sec with metric-scraper
```
Sasha R: run that with two variants: (A) runtime with rrt-2026-11, (B) rollback to rrt-2026-10. Compare avg_batch_size, kernel path, vectors/sec.

Omar K: also check node metrics for CPU steal and memcopy times. If fallback kernel uses extra host <-> device transfers, that will kill throughput even if GPU util seems low.

Lia G: customer also posted a sample failing response showing a 400 with body: 
```json
{"error":"DimensionMismatch: expected 1024, got 1536"}
```
Lia G: they confirmed their client was out-of-date; we asked them to stop sending expected_dim override. But that only affects a subset of their requests. The widespread vectors/sec drop is likely separate.

eng-oncall: quick checklist I'm running now:
- verify kernel-selector logs for quant params existence
- check deploy image tags for runtime on affected hosts
- run Sasha's curl harness on canary with metric capture
- look at batcher config flags: batch_timeout_ms, max_batch_bytes, continuous-batching_v2 enabled?

Sasha R: I noticed batch_timeout_ms was reduced from 12ms to 6ms in the patch (intent was to reduce tail for small chats). That would reduce aggregation for large parallel clients and drop avg_batch_size. That lines up with our numbers.

Omar K: ah — we reduced the timeout to benefit small chat requests, but that had a side-effect on large bulk embedding clients. We can either scope the flag (disable for embeddings route) or bump timeout back and add route-specific tuning.

Lia G: action items:
- Omar to rollback kernel-selector heuristics change on canary and/or re-enable quant-kernel preference (ETA 60m)
- Omar to revert batch_timeout_ms to 12ms on embedding worker pool or add route-specific config (ETA 45m)
- Sasha to run perf harness A/B and post diff (ETA 30m)
- Lia to update customer (Acme) with temporary mitigation steps: set client to not override expected_dim and recommend retry pattern (ETA 15m)
- eng-oncall to collect full nvidia-smi, kernel logs, and batcher traces for affected hosts and attach to INC-7123

support-bot: INC-7123 updated with action items and assigned to Omar K, Sasha R.

Sasha R: quick preliminary run on canary (post revert batch_timeout -> 12ms locally): results: avg_batch_size jumped from 38 -> 124, avg_vectors_per_sec increased from 12k -> 46k, kernel_selector resumed choosing quantized kernel path. Pushing more comprehensive bench now.

Omar K: starting the canary rollback of heuristics now. I'll monitor kernel_selector logs.

Lia G: thanks all. I'll keep Acme in the loop. If the canary looks good, we'll do a fast rollback across hosts for the embedding pool.

eng-oncall: attaching trace ids for later: trace: trc-20261120-abc123, trc-20261120-def456. Saved nvidia-smi sample: 
```
Thu Nov 20 22:12:00 2025
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
|  GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0    A100-SXM4      Off        | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 0%   42C    P0    42W / 400W |   42%   3243MiB / 40960MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Lia G: I'll post a final summary to the ticket after the rollback completes. If anyone sees other customers with similar regressions, please tag this thread.

Omar K: will also add a route-specific flag to prevent batch_timeout tuning from impacting large-batch embedding workloads.

Sasha R: one more note — we should consider adding a fast-detection alert: when avg_batch_size for embedding pool drops >50% AND queue_depth_95p > 3x baseline, auto-revert the batching flag or scale up pool. That would've caught this earlier.

Lia G: agreed. thanks team.

support-bot: INC-7123 status -> in-progress.

(End of thread)
